findings.title: Working-hours check compares a single point (start==end) and uses the wrong logic
findings.body: `end` is computed identically to `start` (`slotStartTime.hour()*60 + minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` is not checking the slot's end. The `.find` returns true if ANY working-hour entry that includes the day has the slot outside its range. With multiple entries per day (split shifts, or multiple aggregate entries) a slot inside one entry is rejected because it's outside another. The check also ignores the organizer timezone/DST (working hours are in UTC minutes, compared against slot UTC time, so day-of-week and day boundaries can be wrong). This can wrongly remove valid slots, or fail to catch slots whose end exceeds working hours.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === (always false)
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object references, so it is never true. The intended handling of zero-length overrides (start equals end, meaning unavailable that day) is dead code. The slot may then be treated as inside the override or only partially excluded.

findings.title: Date override matching mixes organizer-local date with invitee-UTC slot date and ignores later overrides
findings.body: The override date is derived by shifting `date.start` by the negative organizer offset (`-utcOffset`), which is the wrong direction for converting UTC to organizer local (it should be adding +offset), and it is then compared to the slot's UTC date. The offset sign and the frame of reference are inconsistent, so an override can be attributed to the wrong day for non-UTC organizers, and slots on adjacent days may be wrongly accepted or rejected. Also `dateOverrideExist` is set on the first matching override but `find` stops at the first returning true; with several overrides on one day (split ranges) a slot inside the second range is rejected because it fails the first range check.

findings.title: Override offset computed with a single timezone-offset difference breaks across DST and day boundaries
findings.body: The shifted start/end times are reduced to minutes-of-day via `.hour()*60+.minute()`, which discards day rollover: when the offset pushes an override past midnight, startTime/endTime wrap (e.g. end becomes smaller than start), and `buildSlots` skips ranges with `start >= end`, so the override disappears. The `activeOverrides` filter at line 207 still uses the unshifted UTC start for picking the invitee day, so overrides shifted into an adjacent invitee day are neither selected nor placed correctly. Also `override.start.toString()` is used to build the dayjs object, which yields a locale-formatted string with truncated precision and is parsed in server-local time, so the offset can be wrong. `override.timeZone` is optional and, if undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the local zone.

findings.title: New timezone test asserts unchanged behavior and doesn't cover the fix or the fixed-host case
findings.body: The added test expects the identical slots for Asia/Dhaka and Asia/Kolkata, because timeSlots are returned in UTC and the helper compares UTC strings, so it cannot detect whether the override shifted per invitee timezone. The `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher also only uses `.every` over actual slots, so extra or missing expected slots can go unnoticed. No test covers the main fix of the PR (a round-robin event with fixed-host date overrides), nor DST or cross-midnight overrides.
